source_text: Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ἀποπηδᾷν ἀπὸ τῆς μυ σαρᾶς αἱρέσεως τῶν Ἀρειανῶν, τὸ μὴ διαιρεῖν τὴν ἁγίαν Τριάδα, καὶ λέγειν τι ταύτης εἶναι κτίσμα. Οἱ γὰρ προσποιούμενοι μὲν ὀνομάζειν τὴν ὁμολογηθεῖσαν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν, τολμῶντες δὲ κατὰ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος βλασφημεῖν, οὐδὲν πλέον ποιοῦσιν, ἢ τὴν Ἀρειανὴν αἵρεσιν τοῖς μὲν ῥήμασιν ἀρνοῦνται, τῷ δὲ φρονήματι ταύτην κατέχουσιν. Ἀναθεματιζέσθω δὲ παρὰ πάντων ἡ Σαβελλίου καὶ Παύλου τοῦ Σαμοσατέως ἀσέβεια, καὶ Οὐαλεντίνου καὶ Βασιλεί δου ἡ μανία, καὶ τῶν Μανιχαίων ἡ παραφροσύνη· τούτων γὰρ οὕτω γινομένων, πᾶσα παρὰ πάν των ὑποψία φαύλη περιαιρεθήσεται, καὶ μόνη τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἡ πίστις καθαρὰ δειχθήσεται. Ὅτι μὲν οὖν ταύτην ἔχομεν τὴν πίστιν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἀεὶ μεθ' ἡμῶν τὴν κοινωνίαν ἐσχηκότες, οὐδένα οὔτε ὑμῶν οὔθ' ἕτερόν τινα ἀγνοεῖν ἡγούμεθα. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ συγχαίρομεν τοῖς βουλομένοις συνάπτεσθαι, πᾶσι μὲν, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ τοῖς ἐν τῇ Παλαιᾷ συναγομένοις, καὶ μάλιστα τὸν Κύριον ἐδοξάσαμεν, ὡς ἐπὶ πᾶσι, καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀγαθῇ προθέσει τούτων· παρακα λοῦμεν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τούτοις γίνεσθαι τούτων τὴν ὁμόνοιαν, καὶ μηδὲν τούτων πλέον, καθὰ προείπομεν, μήτε τοὺς ἐν τῇ Παλαιᾷ συναγομένους ἀπαιτεῖσθαι παρ' ὑμῶν, μήτε τοὺς περὶ Παυλῖνον ἕτερόν τι μήτε πλέον τῶν ἐν Νικαίᾳ προβάλλεσθαι. Καὶ τὸ θρυληθὲν γοῦν παρά τινων πιττάκιον, ὡς ἐν τῇ κατὰ Σαρδικὴν συνόδῳ συνταχθὲν περὶ πί στεως, κωλύετε κἂν ὅλως ἀναγινώσκεσθαι ἢ προφέρεσθαι· οὐδὲν γὰρ τοιοῦτον ὥρισεν ἡ σύνοδος. Ἠξίω σαν μὲν γάρ τινες, ὡς ἐνδεοῦς οὔσης τῆς κατὰ Νίκαιαν συνόδου, γράψαι περὶ πίστεως, καὶ ἐπεχείρησάν γε προπετῶς· ἡ δὲ ἁγία σύνοδος ἡ ἐν Σαρδικῇ συναχθεῖσα ἠγανάκτησε, καὶ ὥρισε μηδὲν ἔτι περὶ πίστεως γράφεσθαι, ἀλλ' ἀρκεῖσθαι τῇ ἐν Νικαίᾳ παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων ὁμολογηθείσῃ πίστει, διὰ τὸ μηδὲν αὐτῇ λείπειν, ἀλλὰ πλήρη εὐσεβείας εἶναι, καὶ ὅτι μὴ δεῖν δευτέραν ἐκτίθεσθαι πίστιν, ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ γραφεῖσα ὡς ἀτελὴς οὖσα νομισθῇ, καὶ πρόφασις δοθῇ τοῖς ἐθέλουσι πολλάκις γράφειν καὶ ὁρίζειν περὶ πίστεως. Ὅθεν κἂν τοῦτό τις, ἢ ἕτερον προβάλληται, παύετε τοὺς τοιούτους, καὶ μᾶλλον εἰ ρηνεύειν αὐτοὺς πείθετε· καὶ γὰρ οὐδὲν πλέον συνεί δομεν ἐν τούτοις ἢ φιλονεικίαν μόνην. Οὓς γὰρ ἐμέμφοντό τινες ὡς τρεῖς λέγοντας ὑποστάσεις, διὰ τὸ ἀγράφους καὶ ὑπόπτους αὐτόθεν εἶναι τὰς λέξεις, ἠξιώσαμεν μὲν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιζητεῖν πλὴν τῆς κατὰ Νίκαιαν ὁμολογίας· ἀνεκρίναμεν δὲ ὅμως τούτους διὰ τὴν φιλονεικίαν, μὴ ἆρ' ὡς οἱ Ἀρειομανῖται λέγουσιν ἀπηλλοτριωμένας καὶ ἀπεξενωμένας, ἀλλο τριοουσίους τε ἀλλήλων, καὶ ἑκάστην καθ' ἑαυτὴν ὑπόστασιν διῃρημένην, ὡς ἔστι τά τε ἄλλα κτίσματα, καὶ οἱ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γεννώμενοι· ἢ ὥσπερ διαφόρους οὐσίας, ὥσπερ ἐστὶ χρυσὸς, ἢ ἄργυρος, ἢ χαλκὸς, οὕτω καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγωσιν· ἢ ὡς ἄλλοι αἱρετικοὶ τρεῖς ἀρ χὰς καὶ τρεῖς θεοὺς λέγουσιν, οὕτω καὶ οὗτοι φρονοῦν τες, τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις λέγωσι; Διεβεβαιώσαντο μήτε λέγειν, μήτε πεφρονηκέναι ποτὲ οὕτως. Ἐρωτών των δὲ ἡμῶν αὐτούς· Πῶς οὖν ταῦτα λέγετε; ἢ διὰ τί δὲ ὅλως τοιαύταις χρῆσθαι λέξεσιν; ἀπεκρίναντο, διὰ τὸ εἰς ἁγίαν Τριάδα πιστεύειν, οὐκ ὀνόματι Τριάδα μόνον, ἀλλ' ἀληθῶς οὖσαν καὶ ὑφεστῶσαν, Πατέρα τε ἀληθῶς ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα, καὶ Υἱὸν ἀληθῶς ἐνού σιον ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα, καὶ Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ὑφεστὼς καὶ ὑπάρχον οἴδαμεν, μήτε δὲ εἰρηκέναι τρεῖς θεοὺς ἢ τρεῖς ἀρχὰς, μήθ' ὅλως ἀνέχεσθαι τῶν τοῦτο λεγόντων, ἢ φρονούντων· ἀλλ' εἰδέναι ἁγίαν μὲν Τριάδα, μίαν δὲ θεότητα, καὶ μίαν ἀρχὴν, καὶ Υἱὸν μὲν ὁμοούσιον τῷ Πατρὶ, ὡς εἶπον οἱ Πατέρες, τὸ δὲ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα, οὐ κτίσμα, οὐδὲ ξένον, ἀλλ' ἴδιον καὶ ἀδιαίρετον τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ Πατρός.
thought_title: True rejection of Arianism and the Sardican document
orientation: Athanasius and the bishops with him are explaining what true rejection of the Arian heresy requires, and then addressing the rumored Sardican document about faith.
pass_a_gloss: For this is truly to leap away from the abominable heresy of the Arians: not to divide the holy Trinity, and to say that something of it is a creature. For those who pretend to name the faith confessed at Nicaea, but dare to blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, do nothing more than deny the Arian heresy in words, but hold it in their mind. Let the impiety of Sabellius and Paul of Samosata be condemned by all, and the madness of Valentinus and Basilides, and the derangement of the Manichaeans; for when these things happen thus, every base suspicion among all will be removed, and the faith of the catholic Church alone will be shown pure. That we and those who have always had communion with us hold this faith, we think no one, neither of you nor anyone else, is ignorant. Since we rejoice with those who wish to be joined, with all indeed, but especially with those who gather in the Old Church, we glorified the Lord most of all, as in all things, also in the good purpose of these; we urge you to bring about their concord on these terms, and nothing more than these, as we said before, neither to require from those who gather in the Old Church, nor for those around Paulinus to put forward anything else or more than the things at Nicaea. And the document that has been talked about by some, as having been composed at the council at Sardica about faith, forbid it to be read or produced at all; for the council decreed no such thing. For some demanded, as if the council at Nicaea were deficient, to write about faith, and they attempted it rashly; but the holy council gathered at Sardica was indignant, and decreed that nothing further be written about faith, but that the faith confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers be sufficient, because nothing is lacking to it, but it is full of piety, and that it is not necessary to set forth a second faith, lest the one written at Nicaea be considered as incomplete, and an occasion be given to those who wish often to write and decree about faith. Wherefore if anyone puts forward this or another, stop such people, and rather persuade them to be at peace; for indeed we know nothing more in these matters than mere love of strife. For those whom some blamed as saying three persons, because the words were unwritten and suspicious in themselves, we asked that nothing more be sought beyond the confession at Nicaea; but we examined them nevertheless because of the love of strife, whether perhaps as the Arians say, alienated and estranged, different in being from one another, and each person divided by itself, as are the other creatures and those born from human beings; or as different beings, as is gold, or silver, or bronze, so also they say; or as other heretics say three principles and three gods, so also these, thinking thus, say three persons? They affirmed that they neither say nor have ever thought thus. When we asked them: How then do you say these things? Or why do you use such words at all? They answered, because they believe in a holy Trinity, not a Trinity in name only, but truly existing and subsisting, a Father truly existing and subsisting, and a Son truly same in being and subsisting, and we know the Holy Spirit subsisting and existing, and they have neither said three gods or three principles, nor do they at all tolerate those who say or think this; but they know a holy Trinity, and one divinity, and one principle, and the Son same in being with the Father, as the Fathers said, and the Holy Spirit is not a creature, nor foreign, but proper to and inseparable from the being of the Son and of the Father.

choices.english: to leap away from the abominable heresy
choices.why: ἀποπηδᾷν is a vivid verb of jumping or springing away; 'leap away' preserves the force of decisive separation.

choices.term: τὸ μὴ διαιρεῖν τὴν ἁγίαν Τριάδα
choices.english: not to divide the holy Trinity
choices.why: The articular infinitive with μή expresses the content of true rejection; 'not to divide' keeps the negative force and the infinitive's explanatory role.
rejected: the not dividing of the holy Trinity

choices.why: The glossary requires 'condemn' for ἀναθεματίζειν; the third-person imperative is rendered with 'let it be' to preserve the command's impersonal force.
The glossary requires 'document' for πιττάκιον, avoiding 'formula' or 'paper'.
ἐνούσιον is a technical term meaning 'in being' or 'consubstantial'; rendering it 'same in being' aligns with the glossary's treatment of ὁμοούσιος and preserves the Nicene sense.

choices.term: ἴδιον καὶ ἀδιαίρετον τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ Πατρός
choices.english: proper to and inseparable from the being of the Son and of the Father
choices.why: ἴδιον means 'proper to' or 'belonging to', and ἀδιαίρετον means 'inseparable from'; the genitive τῆς οὐσίας must be rendered explicitly to preserve the claim about the Spirit's relation to the divine being.
rejected: proper and indivisible of the being

pass_b_english: For this is truly to leap away from the abominable heresy of the Arians: not to divide the holy Trinity, and to say that any part of it is a creature. Those who pretend to name the faith confessed at Nicaea but dare to blaspheme against the Holy Spirit do nothing more than deny the Arian heresy in words while holding to it in their minds. Let the impiety of Sabellius and Paul of Samosata be condemned by all, and the madness of Valentinus and Basilides, and the derangement of the Manichaeans. For when these things are done, every evil suspicion will be removed from all, and the faith of the catholic Church alone will be shown to be pure.

We believe that no one, neither you nor anyone else, is ignorant that we and those who have always shared communion with us hold this faith. But since we rejoice with those who wish to be joined to us—with all of them, and especially with those who gather in the Old Church—we glorified the Lord especially, as in all things, and for the good purpose of these people. We urge you to bring about their unity on these terms, and nothing more than these, as we said before: neither require anything more from those who gather in the Old Church, nor let those around Paulinus put forward anything else or anything beyond what was decided at Nicaea.

And as for the document rumored by some to have been composed about the faith at the Council of Sardica, forbid it to be read or produced at all. For the council decreed no such thing. Some did request that a statement about the faith be written, on the grounds that the Council of Nicaea was deficient, and they attempted this rashly. But the holy council that gathered at Sardica was indignant, and it decreed that nothing further should be written about the faith, but that the faith confessed by the Fathers at Nicaea should suffice, because it lacks nothing and is full of piety, and because a second faith should not be set forth, lest the one written at Nicaea be thought incomplete, and a pretext be given to those who wish to write and decree about the faith repeatedly. Therefore, if anyone puts forward this document or another one, stop such people, and rather persuade them to be at peace. For we agreed that there was nothing more in these matters than mere love of contention.

As for those whom some criticized for speaking of three persons, because the terms were unwritten and therefore suspect, we asked that nothing more be required beyond the confession of Nicaea. Nevertheless, because of the contention, we examined them: did they perhaps say, as the Arians say, that the persons are alienated and estranged from one another, foreign in being to each other, and each person divided by itself, as are the other creatures and those born from human beings? Or did they speak of different beings, as gold, silver, or bronze differ? Or, as other heretics speak of three principles and three gods, did these men think that way and speak of three persons? They affirmed that they neither said nor ever thought such things.

When we asked them, 'How then do you say these things? Or why do you use such terms at all?' they answered: 'Because we believe in a holy Trinity, not a Trinity in name only, but one that truly exists and subsists—a Father who truly is and subsists, a Son who truly is same in being and subsists, and a Holy Spirit who subsists and exists; this we know.' They added that they had never spoken of three gods or three principles, nor did they at all tolerate those who say or think such things, but that they knew a holy Trinity, one divinity, and one principle, and that the Son is same in being with the Father, as the Fathers said, and that the Holy Spirit was not a creature, nor foreign, but proper to and inseparable from the being of the Son and of the Father.

συνείδομεν means 'we agreed/concurred', not 'we found'. The bishops agreed among themselves. Fixed to 'we agreed that there was nothing more'.

fixed.quote: we know that they had not said that there are three gods or three principles, nor did they at all tolerate those who say or think such things, but that they knew a holy Trinity
fixed.fix: this we know.' They added that they had never spoken of three gods or three principles, nor did they at all tolerate those who say or think such things, but that they knew a holy Trinity
fixed.note: οἴδαμεν ends the clause about the Spirit, and the infinitives that follow report what the speakers said, so 'we know that they had not said' wrongly makes the report Athanasius's own claim; the checker's 'direct speech' reading is also wrong.

dismissed.quote: and that the Son is same in being with the Father, as the Fathers said, and that the Holy Spirit was not a creature
dismissed.why: Continues first-person direct speech: 'the Son is same in being... the Spirit is not a creature.' English wrongly shifts to indirect third-person 'that the Son is... that the Spirit was.'
dismissed.note: From εἰρηκέναι onward the Greek is indirect speech, so reported 'that the Son is… that the Spirit was' is a fair rendering.

dismissed.quote: and that the Holy Spirit was not a creature, nor foreign, but proper to and inseparable from the being of the Son and of the Father
dismissed.why: Direct speech of opponents continues but English shifts to past tense narration, obscuring who speaks.
dismissed.note: Past tense is a normal English shift for reported speech after ἀπεκρίναντο; the meaning is unchanged.
